image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and upper back emerging from blue ocean water. The skin is dark grey with distinctive white mottling (barnacles/lice). The arched rostrum and blowholes are visible at the surface. No dorsal fin is present, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic arched rostrum and the blowhole area breaking the surface. The proportions match the 'short head' description relative to the massive body implied.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing the specific grey base color with scattered white/light grey patches typical of cyamid infestations and barnacles found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the absence of a dorsal fin is consistent with the visible portion, the 'multiple dorsal knuckles' are located further down the back which is submerged or out of frame in this close-up crop. Cannot fully verify the knuckle count/structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section of the whale is visible. The full spindle shape and total proportions cannot be verified from this cropped perspective.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; the visible skin exhibits the correct mottling pattern.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally and posterior to the head; they are completely submerged and out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture on the head shows the rough, uneven surface characteristic of callosities and barnacle clusters.
